# watchpoint_monitor_policy (Resource)

Cross-region down confirmation and the owning team for one monitor of any type. These settings are written through the platform's bulk monitor endpoint and are not returned by the monitor reads, so a change made in the portal is not detected as drift. Destroying the resource resets confirmation to `None` and clears the owner.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Only page when at least two regions agree the API is down, and file the
# monitor under the platform team.
resource "watchpoint_monitor_policy" "api" {
  monitor_id          = watchpoint_http_monitor.api.id
  confirmation_policy = "Quorum"
  quorum_min_regions  = 2
  owner_group_id      = watchpoint_user_group.platform.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `monitor_id` (String) ID of the monitor (any type) the settings apply to.

### Optional

- `confirmation_policy` (String) `None` (every failing result counts), `ConfirmFromAnotherRegion` (a failure is re-run from a different region and counts only if that fails too) or `Quorum` (down only while at least `quorum_min_regions` regions are failing). Defaults to `None`. Anything that cannot confirm, such as a private location, counts the failure as before.
- `owner_group_id` (String) Owning team (a `watchpoint_user_group` id). A filter label; it grants no access.
- `quorum_min_regions` (Number) Failing regions needed for `Quorum`, between `2` and `20`. Capped at the number of regions the check actually runs from.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same as `monitor_id`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import watchpoint_monitor_policy.api <monitor_id>
```
